answer: An agent marketplace can issue each participant a one-time, non-transferable credential after an audited organization verifies a real operator. For each epoch, a zero-knowledge proof shows possession of the credential secret and derives a public nullifier from that epoch; validators reject duplicate nullifiers without learning a name. The signal, kernel, and cipher fields in a job receipt are hashed into the proof, so replay across jobs fails. Creating n aliases requires n distinct verified operators and their coordination cost; copying keys yields no extra claim.
